a frequency-domain TEQ approach can achieve the objectives of channel and/or echo shortening as well as noise and/or interference suppression in the DMT transceiver.

we have developed a frequency-domain approach to the equalization and noise-suppression problems, which is applicable to both the DMT system with frequency division multiplexed subcarriers and the echo-cancellation based DMT system.

the frequency-domain TEQS can be used to control the spectral characteristics of the DMT system in a way that is not possible with the time-domain TEQs and that they can be used to shorten the channel or the channel and echo response, as well as to suppress the noise or the interference in the DTM system, all in an efficient way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of a frequency-domain TEQ for DMT systems, which is capable of suppressing the noise and interference, and can be used to shorten the channel and echo response jointly.
the design and analysis of the TEQ in the frequency-domain.

developing a frequency-domain TEQ training algorithm that can be used for both equalization and noise/interference suppression in the DMT systems, and the simulation results show that the algorithm can achieve the desired objectives effectively.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a frequency-domain TEQ approach, which is more effective in terms of shortening and noise suppression than the existing time-domain approach.
our frequency-domain approach is a powerful tool for the design of the TEQ and its extensions for the DMT transceiver.
the frequency-domain TEQS are effective and efficient in achieving the objectives of channel and/or echo shortening, as well as noise and interference suppression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frequency-domain TEQC can be used for the DMT transceivers to shorten the channel impulse response and to suppress the noise in a joint manner.
, in DMT systems, a frequency-domain approach is not only a viable alternative to the time-domain approach, but also a more flexible and powerful one.

a frequency-domain training approach can be used to design a TEQ for the DMT systems, with a weighting function that allows the TEQ to be used as a filter to suppress the noise or interference in the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequency-domain approach can be used to solve the TEQ problem in the DMT transceivers, and it can also be used to solve some other problems in the DMT systems.
the frequency-domain TEQC can be used to achieve the shortening and noise suppression objectives in a single framework.
the frequency-domain TEQS design approach is a powerful and flexible tool for the DMT transceiver design, and the weighted frequency-domain approach is especially useful in the DMT systems.
